assumptions._note: GAM Research forecast drivers for Bayer CropScience Ltd (standalone; no subsidiaries; Rs crore). One reportable segment (crop protection ~76%, hybrid corn seed ~19%, other ~5%). Revenue grows at a single rate; the business-line build (corn vs crop protection) is checked in the authoring script. EBITDA margin is a driver; treasury income = yield x opening cash and liquid funds net of lease liabilities. Valued on P/E, as the street does.
assumptions._revenueWhy: FY27: Q1 -4% (weather, lower acreage; corn held up); the June-September monsoon ended 12.6% below normal (IMD), kharif maize area ~4% below last year at 21-Aug and southern reservoirs ~33% below normal before a rabi season with El Nino expected to persist to Feb-2027; flubendiamide rights sold (Apr-2026). Q2FY26 was a weak base (excess rain, -11%), so we assume H1 about -3% and H2 about -3%. FY28-29: normal monsoons, corn seed +12-14% a year, crop protection +6-7% with launches (Bicota, Camalus, Etciostar, Xivana Smart, Plenexos later). Below management's 'high single to low double digit' aspiration; in line with its FY21-26 record of ~6% a year.

base._why: FY26 turnover Rs 5,675 cr split with the BRSR shares (corn seed 19%, crop protection 76% + other 5%); rounded, so approximate.

businessLines._why: Corn: Q1FY27 held up despite ~4% lower kharif maize area; rabi risk from southern reservoirs; then +13% a year (FY21-25: ~15%; management: double again over ~5 years). Crop protection and other: -4.9% in FY27 (deficient monsoon, flubendiamide rights sold, older products divested), then +6-7% with launches. The authoring script checks that the two lines sum to model revenue.

assumptions._marginWhy: 15.4% in FY26 (12.6% in FY25, 18-19% in FY23-24 when glyphosate prices spiked). Q1FY27 20.0% (18.2%) on price increases and mix. Management guided ~+100bp a year from FY25 for 2-3 years and has already delivered +280bp; more local sourcing, lower receivable write-offs and the partner go-to-market model help, but a falling top line in FY27 and Chinese generic pricing cap it. We stay below the FY20-24 average (~18.6%).
assumptions._capexWhy: Cash capex Rs 43-77 cr a year in FY22-26 (Rs 64 cr in FY26, incl. Rs 39 cr of R&D capital) plus Rs 26-107 cr a year of new leased assets (warehouses, vehicles), which depreciate like capex. We include ~Rs 40 cr a year of leases so depreciation does not fall artificially.
assumptions._depWhy: FY26 depreciation and amortisation Rs 94 cr (incl. Rs 55 cr on right-of-use assets) = 10.4% of average gross block (Rs 902 cr, Screener).
assumptions._treasuryWhy: Applied to opening cash and liquid funds net of lease liabilities (Rs 1,397 cr at Mar-26). March is the seasonal peak; cash falls through the year as dealers are given credit and two dividends are paid. FY26 treasury income (deposit interest Rs 32.5 cr + mutual-fund gains Rs 15.6 cr) was ~5.9% of the opening net balance.
assumptions._otherIncomeWhy: Non-treasury other income: rent from group companies (~Rs 13 cr) and penal interest on overdue dealer receivables (~Rs 10 cr) recur; FY27 adds the Rs 63.9 cr gain on selling the flubendiamide marketing rights (Q1FY27). Profit on divesting products (Rs 22-27 cr a year in FY25-26) is not assumed to recur.
assumptions._interestWhy: Rs 20 cr in FY26: lease interest (Rs 8 cr) and interest on employee benefits/MSME dues; no borrowings.
assumptions._taxWhy: Effective 19.4% in FY26 and 19.7% in FY25: income from producing corn seed is claimed as tax-exempt agricultural income (Rs 64.6 cr tax saving in FY26), under dispute (Rs 233 cr contingent).
assumptions._payoutWhy: Dividends were 77-105% of EPS in FY22-26 (Rs 150 a share for FY26, ~98%); management said the dividend distribution 'remains intact' through the FY25 dip. The promoter group (71.4%) receives ~71% of it.

dcf._betaWhy: Debt-free with net cash; earnings swing with the monsoon but the parent's support and dividend record lower the risk: slightly below market sensitivity (Ke 11.6%).
dcf._tgWhy: Indian crop protection and seed demand grows with farm output and prices; 5.5% nominal, below the 6% we use for faster-growing peers because ~95% of profit is paid out.
dcf._fadeGrowthWhy: Industry growth of 5-6% plus corn seed share gains.
dcf._fadeCapexWhy: Asset-light formulator and seed producer: capex (incl. leases) ~2% of sales.

bull.label: Bull
bull.narrative: A normal rabi and 2027 monsoon; corn seed keeps growing ~15% and new molecules (Xivana Smart, Plenexos) scale; local sourcing lifts gross margin; margin ~18%.

bear.label: Bear
bear.narrative: El Nino hurts the rabi and the 2027 kharif; glyphosate use restricted; Chinese generic prices fall again and receivable write-offs return; margin ~15%.

methods.name: P/E
methods.why: How the street values Bayer CropScience (HSBC 29x FY27E EPS; Kotak method not disclosed). 24x = its 31.7x one-year-forward median since Apr-2021, cut by the ~20% de-rating of domestic crop-protection peers (Sumitomo, PI, Dhanuka, Rallis) to ~25.5x, and by ~5% because our FY26-29E EPS growth (~6%) is a little below the ~7% it delivered while trading at 31.7x. Bull 28x (its 25th percentile since 2021); bear 19x (dividend-discount value at an 11.6% cost of equity).

methods.name: EV/EBITDA
methods.why: Values the business and the net cash separately. 16x Sep-28E EBITDA = its ~25x trailing EV/EBITDA median since Apr-2021, less the same ~20% de-rating and ~5% growth discount (~19x trailing), restated on EBITDA two years ahead (+18%).

methods.name: DCF
methods.why: Tests whether cash flows support the price: 15-year FCFF, Ke 11.6%, terminal growth 5.5%, plus net cash.

cover.headline: A de-rated Bayer franchise with a corn-seed engine: cheap enough, just, despite a weak season
cover.lead: Bayer CropScience is the Indian listed arm of Bayer AG (71.4% owned): crop protection (~76% of FY26 turnover), DEKALB hybrid corn seed (~19%) and small exports. It has no debt, ₹1,479 cr of cash at Mar-2026 and pays out almost all its profit (₹150 a share for FY26). The shares have fallen 28% from their 52-week high to ₹3,628; Q1FY27 revenue fell 4% and the 2026 monsoon ended 12.6% below normal. The street values the stock on **P/E** (HSBC: 29x FY27E). We forecast EPS of ₹162.0 in FY27E (core profit down slightly; a one-off gain lifts the reported figure) and ₹166.0 in FY28E. Applying **24x to Sep-28E EPS of ₹174.5** gives **{{dcf.tp|inr}} ({{dcf.upside|chg}})**: **we initiate with BUY**, only just above our +15% line. The cross-checks are lower (EV/EBITDA ₹3,993, DCF ₹3,396), so this is a valuation call, not a growth call. Bull case {{scen.bull.tp|inr}}; bear case {{scen.bear.tp|inr}}.

arguments.h: The price already assumes little growth
arguments.p: At ₹3,628 the stock trades at 21.9x our FY28E EPS, against a 31.7x one-year-forward median since Apr-2021, and yields ~4.2% on our FY27E dividend. Even after cutting that median for the sector's ~20% de-rating and slightly lower growth, 24x leaves {{dcf.upside|chg}}.

arguments.h: Corn seed is the engine; crop protection is not
arguments.p: Corn seed revenue grew from ₹514 cr (FY21) to ₹914 cr (FY25), ~15% a year, and reached ~19% of FY26 turnover; crop protection excluding Roundup grew ~6% a year. Corn earns more and its seed-production profit is taxed as exempt agricultural income (implied ~₹257 cr in FY26).

Half of all purchases are from Bayer group companies; Bayer AG alone supplied ₹1,341 cr in FY26 (₹2,421 cr in FY25). When imported input costs rose and Chinese generics capped prices, the EBITDA margin fell to 12.6% (FY25). More local sourcing is management's main margin lever, but the parent decides its pace.

arguments.h: The near term is weak, and the cross-checks are cautious
arguments.p: Q1FY27 profit rose 15% only because of a ₹63.9 cr gain on selling the flubendiamide rights; core profit fell ~2%. The monsoon was deficient and El Niño threatens the rabi season. Our DCF (₹3,396) is below the price: the upside depends on the market paying a de-rated, but still premium, multiple again.

catalysts: Q2FY27 results (due by mid-November 2026): how much the deficient monsoon cut kharif sales, and the first FY27 interim dividend (₹90 a share last year).
The rabi season (November-March) under El Niño: southern reservoirs were a third below normal in late September, which matters for rabi corn seed.
New molecules: Xivana Smart (fruit and vegetables) and Plenexos (insecticide) registrations and launches; corn hybrids for new states.
Glyphosate: the Delhi High Court case on restricting use; the paraquat ban (final order 22-Sep-2026) should help Roundup.
Sourcing and transfer prices: purchases from Bayer AG, and the FY28 related-party limit (₹3,500 cr) approved at the August AGM.

sections.title: Bayer's Indian arm: crop protection, DEKALB corn seed, and an agent for the group

blocks.p: Bayer CropScience Ltd (BCSL) sells Bayer's crop-protection products and corn seed to Indian farmers through ~3,500 distributors and their retailers. **Crop protection** (insecticides, fungicides, herbicides, seed treatment, biologicals) is about three-quarters of turnover: many products are formulated at Himatnagar (Gujarat) from technical-grade ingredients bought from Bayer AG and group companies; others are bought finished. **Corn seed** (DEKALB and Xellano hybrids, from the Monsanto India merger of 2019) is ~19%: BCSL breeds hybrids at its own R&D centre and pays contract farmers to grow seed. The rest is Roundup (glyphosate), exports (₹297 cr in FY26, mostly to group companies in Germany and Bangladesh), traded rice seed, and group seed products sold as an agent.

sections.title: A ₹31,000 cr crop-protection market growing 5-6%, and a corn market set to double

blocks.p: India's crop-protection market was ~₹30,800 cr in FY25 and CRISIL expects 5-6% a year to FY28. Use per hectare is low (~0.6 kg vs ~3 kg in the US), but demand in any year depends on the monsoon, pests and crop prices, and Chinese generics set prices for most old molecules. Global innovators (Bayer, Syngenta, BASF, Corteva, FMC, Sumitomo) compete with Indian companies (UPL, PI, Coromandel, Rallis, Dhanuka) and hundreds of generic formulators. Corn is different: India grows ~37 MMT on 11-12 m ha at 3.7 t/ha (world 5.8), and demand from poultry feed, starch and ethanol is expected to reach ~70 MMT by 2030. More corn means more hybrid seed, and better hybrids are the main way to lift yields because there is little new land.

bullets: **Market position.** "We are the main breeders in the country," says the MD; DEKALB and Xellano hybrids came with the Monsanto India merger (2019). FY26 brought five new hybrids (DKC9256, DKC8174, 9243C, DKC9248 for spring, DKC9247), four hybrids notified by the national maize programme and eight plant-variety certificates.

**Growth.** Corn revenue rose from ₹514 cr to ₹914 cr in FY21-25 with both volume and price (a "nearly double-digit" price increase in H1FY26). Management expects it to double again as corn demand doubles by 2030. In Q1FY27 corn "held up well" though kharif maize area was ~4% lower.

**Profitability.** Corn seed has "a slightly higher margin than the CP portfolio and carries a lower cost to serve" and is fully backward integrated except licence costs (royalty to Monsanto Technology ₹22.3 cr in FY26). The tax note implies ~₹257 cr of income treated as agricultural in FY26, a rough proxy for seed profit (~24% of our ~₹1,078 cr corn revenue estimate).

**Costs and risks.** Seed-grower payments doubled to ~₹541 cr in FY25 and stayed there in FY26 as more companies compete for professional growers; Bayer holds more safety stock. Duty-free US corn imports for ethanol, a GM-corn decision that favours rival trait owners, or a bad rabi season (southern reservoirs ~33% below normal) would hit this business.

blocks.callout: **Our view:** corn is the best thing in Bayer CropScience, and the main reason we expect profit growth after FY27. We model corn revenue +5% in FY27 (weather) and +13% a year after; it rises to ~23% of revenue by FY29E. At ~19% of revenue, even 15% growth adds only ~3 points to group growth.

bullets: **Portfolio.** Insecticides, herbicides and fungicides for rice, vegetables, cotton, wheat, soybean and sugarcane; top brands named in Nov-2025: Roundup, Nativo, Laudis, Council Activ. Products launched in the last three years were ~one-sixth of FY25 crop-protection sales; Council Activ (FY23) is a top-2/3 product.

**Launches.** FY26: Bicota (rice stem borer); Camalus (vegetable insecticide); Council Prime (rice herbicide, N&E India); Etciostar (pre-emergent rice herbicide for direct-seeded rice); Mateno More (3-way wheat herbicide); Yeoval (sugarcane early shoot borer). Pipeline: Xivana Smart (fruit and vegetable, 'beginning of next year' subject to MRLs); Plenexos (new insecticide, Bayer 'global blockbuster', 'next couple of years').

**Pruning.** Bayer is selling older products to focus on margin: profit on divestments ₹27 cr (FY25) and ₹22 cr (FY26), and the flubendiamide marketing rights went to Tagros Chemicals for a ₹63.9 cr gain in Q1FY27. Each sale lifts margin but shrinks revenue.

**Pricing.** In FY25 input costs rose while Chinese supply stopped Bayer raising prices ("a perfect storm"); in FY26 input prices stabilised and gross margin rose by more than 100bp in H1. Q1FY27 gained from price increases and mix.

**Go-to-market.** In rice-growing eastern states, partners (Better Life Farming centres, FPOs) now serve farmers instead of Bayer's own field force; sales commission rose to ₹89 cr (₹21 cr in FY25) while employee costs fell.

blocks.callout: **Our view:** this is a solid, branded, market-rate business, not a growth story. Crop protection ex-Roundup grew ~6% a year in FY21-25, in line with the market, and the company is deliberately giving up revenue for margin. We model crop protection and other revenue −5% in FY27 and +7%/+6% after.

blocks.callout: **Our view:** the parent is the moat and the main risk at once. Its molecules and germplasm give BCSL products Indian generic makers cannot sell, and its ~100% dividend policy returns cash to minorities too. But transfer prices decide the margin, the parent sets the pace of local sourcing, and minorities have no say on either. FY26's margin recovery came with purchases from Bayer AG falling 45%; whether that continues is the swing factor for our forecasts.

blocks.callout: **Honest verdict:** Bayer CropScience has a **narrow moat**. In corn it has the best germplasm and brand in India, a lead that takes rivals years of breeding to close. In crop protection it has premium brands and first access to Bayer's new chemistry, but most revenue is in molecules that generics can copy, its cost base is tied to imports from the parent, and growth has only matched the market. Its high ROE comes from paying out all profit, not from compounding. That deserves a premium to Indian generic makers, not the 30x+ the stock used to command.

sections.title: A kharif business: the June quarter alone makes ~40% of the profit

blocks.p: Indian farmers buy most crop protection and corn seed for the kharif (monsoon) season, sown in June-July. Bayer CropScience ships early, so April-June (Q1) is its biggest quarter: in FY26 it brought 34% of revenue and 40% of net profit, and April-September 61% of revenue. October-March covers the rabi (winter) crops: wheat herbicides and rabi/spring corn in the south and east. The pattern explains Q2FY26 (−11%, when rain did not stop and farmers missed sprays) and Q1FY27 (−4%, a weak, late monsoon).

pair.title: Quarterly revenue: the June quarter is the peak
Quarterly net profit

blocks.callout: **The current season is weak:** Q1FY27 revenue fell 4% even before the June-September monsoon ended 12.6% below normal (IMD), with June 35% short. Net profit rose 15%, but ₹64 cr of the ₹89 cr other income was a one-off gain on selling the flubendiamide marketing rights; without it profit fell ~2%. With El Niño expected to last until February 2027 and southern reservoirs a third below normal, the rabi season is also at risk.

sections.title: Six years of ~6% growth, one bad year, and a margin still below its old level

blocks.p: Bayer CropScience's revenue rose from ₹4,261 cr in FY21 to ₹5,675 cr in FY26, about 6% a year, almost all of it from corn seed: crop protection grew less than 6% a year. Profit peaked at ₹758 cr in FY23, when a global shortage lifted glyphosate prices, then fell to ₹568 cr in FY25 (EPS −23%) as input costs rose, Chinese generics stopped Bayer raising prices, dealers paid late and a restructuring cost money. FY26 recovered to ₹689 cr (+21%) on a 15.4% EBITDA margin, still below the 18-20% of FY20-24.

blocks.callout: **Our view:** this is a slow-growing, cash-generative business. ROE of 20-28% looks excellent, but it is high mainly because the company pays out ~100% of profit and keeps equity small, not because it is compounding. Over FY21-26 EPS grew ~7% a year. Future profit growth needs either faster corn growth or a margin back near 18%, and the FY25 shock showed how quickly the margin can fall.

sections.title: Earnings quality: clean audit and real cash, but big estimates, one-offs and a tax dispute

bullets: **Rebates, discounts and returns.** Revenue is shown after ₹900 cr of discounts and ₹123 cr of expected returns (together ~15% of the ₹6,542 cr contracted price). Refund liabilities were ₹666 cr at Mar-2026 (₹571 cr a year earlier), and expected returns rose 51%. The auditor calls the estimate "complex, subjective and susceptible to material misstatement" (key audit matter).
**Receivables.** Expected-credit-loss charges were ₹78 cr in FY25 ("unprecedented" collection problems) and ₹33 cr in FY26; the company also earned ₹9.6 cr of penal interest on overdue dealer bills.
**One-offs in other income.** Profit on selling products: ₹26.8 cr (FY25), ₹22.3 cr (FY26) and the ₹63.9 cr flubendiamide gain in Q1FY27. We treat them as non-recurring.

**Tax.** The 19-20% tax rate depends on treating seed-production income as exempt agricultural income (₹64.6 cr of tax saved in FY26). ₹233 cr of that position is disputed up to the Supreme Court; indirect-tax demands rose to ₹472 cr. A Kerala suit seeks ₹162 cr jointly from Bayer and 15 other endosulfan makers.
**Agency revenue.** Group seed products sold as an agent are booked net (₹322 cr of gross purchases in FY26), which flatters margin percentages slightly but not profit.
**Inventory.** ₹27.2 cr of inventory was written down in FY26 (₹7.6 cr in FY25); 289 inventory days (Screener) make write-downs a recurring risk in bad seasons.
**Cash conversion is good.** Operating cash flow was ₹1,078 cr in FY26 (156% of profit) and ₹3,804 cr over FY21-26 against ₹3,893 cr of profit; FY25 was weak (₹262 cr) when inventory rose ₹821 cr.

blocks.callout: **Accounting flag: AMBER.** Deloitte Haskins & Sells' opinion is unqualified and profits turn into cash over time. The amber is for the size of the rebate and return estimates (~12% of revenue sits in refund liabilities), recurring "one-off" divestment gains, and a tax rate that rests on a disputed exemption.

sections.title: No debt, ₹1,480 cr of cash at the March peak, and heavy inventory

blocks.p: Bayer CropScience has no borrowings, only ₹82 cr of lease liabilities. At Mar-2026 it held ₹1,479 cr of bank balances, liquid funds and investments (₹929 cr a year earlier). March is the seasonal high point: dealers pay before the year end and suppliers are owed a lot, and cash then falls as stock is built and credit given for kharif and two dividends (₹90 in December, ₹60 after the August AGM) are paid. Over FY21-26 operating cash flow was ₹3,804 cr, capex ₹327 cr and dividends ₹3,481 cr: nearly everything left over is paid out. The weak spot is inventory: 289 inventory days in FY26 (319 in FY25, Screener basis), because seed is produced a season ahead and technical-grade chemicals are imported from the parent months before use.

sections.title: Our honest summary: a good franchise at a fair-to-cheap price, bought for the multiple, not the growth

blocks.callout: **What you are buying:** India's leading corn-seed breeder (DEKALB), first access to Bayer's new crop-protection chemistry, premium brands, no debt, ₹1,479 cr of cash at the March peak, ROE ~24% and a ~4.2% dividend yield on our FY27E payout.

**What you are paying:** 21.9x our FY28E EPS, against a 31.7x forward median since 2021, for a company growing ~6-7% a year whose crop-protection book only keeps pace with the market and whose margin depends on its parent's transfer prices. On the street's method and our inputs the target is {{dcf.tp|inr}} ({{dcf.upside|chg}}), just above our +15% BUY line; the DCF says the price is roughly fair. This is a low-conviction BUY.

assumptions._note: GAM Research forecast drivers for Bayer CropScience Ltd (standalone; no subsidiaries; Rs crore). One reportable segment (crop protection ~76%, hybrid corn seed ~19%, other ~5%). Revenue grows at a single rate; the business-line build (corn vs crop protection) is checked in the authoring script. EBITDA margin is a driver; treasury income = yield x opening cash and liquid funds net of lease liabilities. Valued on P/E, as the street does.
assumptions._revenueWhy: FY27: Q1 -4% (weather, lower acreage; corn held up); the June-September monsoon ended 12.6% below normal (IMD), kharif maize area ~4% below last year at 21-Aug and southern reservoirs ~33% below normal before a rabi season with El Nino expected to persist to Feb-2027; flubendiamide rights sold (Apr-2026). Q2FY26 was a weak base (excess rain, -11%), so we assume H1 about -3% and H2 about -3%. FY28-29: normal monsoons, corn seed +12-14% a year, crop protection +6-7% with launches (Bicota, Camalus, Etciostar, Xivana Smart, Plenexos later). Below management's 'high single to low double digit' aspiration; in line with its FY21-26 record of ~6% a year.

base._why: FY26 turnover Rs 5,675 cr split with the BRSR shares (corn seed 19%, crop protection 76% + other 5%); rounded, so approximate.

businessLines._why: Corn: Q1FY27 held up despite ~4% lower kharif maize area; rabi risk from southern reservoirs; then +13% a year (FY21-25: ~15%; management: double again over ~5 years). Crop protection and other: -4.9% in FY27 (deficient monsoon, flubendiamide rights sold, older products divested), then +6-7% with launches. The authoring script checks that the two lines sum to model revenue.

assumptions._marginWhy: 15.4% in FY26 (12.6% in FY25, 18-19% in FY23-24 when glyphosate prices spiked). Q1FY27 20.0% (18.2%) on price increases and mix. Management guided ~+100bp a year from FY25 for 2-3 years and has already delivered +280bp; more local sourcing, lower receivable write-offs and the partner go-to-market model help, but a falling top line in FY27 and Chinese generic pricing cap it. We stay below the FY20-24 average (~18.6%).
assumptions._capexWhy: Cash capex Rs 43-77 cr a year in FY22-26 (Rs 64 cr in FY26, incl. Rs 39 cr of R&D capital) plus Rs 26-107 cr a year of new leased assets (warehouses, vehicles), which depreciate like capex. We include ~Rs 40 cr a year of leases so depreciation does not fall artificially.
assumptions._depWhy: FY26 depreciation and amortisation Rs 94 cr (incl. Rs 55 cr on right-of-use assets) = 10.4% of average gross block (Rs 902 cr, Screener).
assumptions._treasuryWhy: Applied to opening cash and liquid funds net of lease liabilities (Rs 1,397 cr at Mar-26). March is the seasonal peak; cash falls through the year as dealers are given credit and two dividends are paid. FY26 treasury income (deposit interest Rs 32.5 cr + mutual-fund gains Rs 15.6 cr) was ~5.9% of the opening net balance.
assumptions._otherIncomeWhy: Non-treasury other income: rent from group companies (~Rs 13 cr) and penal interest on overdue dealer receivables (~Rs 10 cr) recur; FY27 adds the Rs 63.9 cr gain on selling the flubendiamide marketing rights (Q1FY27). Profit on divesting products (Rs 22-27 cr a year in FY25-26) is not assumed to recur.
assumptions._interestWhy: Rs 20 cr in FY26: lease interest (Rs 8 cr) and interest on employee benefits/MSME dues; no borrowings.
assumptions._taxWhy: Effective 19.4% in FY26 and 19.7% in FY25: income from producing corn seed is claimed as tax-exempt agricultural income (Rs 64.6 cr tax saving in FY26), under dispute (Rs 233 cr contingent).
assumptions._payoutWhy: Dividends were 77-105% of EPS in FY22-26 (Rs 150 a share for FY26, ~98%); management said the dividend distribution 'remains intact' through the FY25 dip. The promoter group (71.4%) receives ~71% of it.

dcf._betaWhy: Debt-free with net cash; earnings swing with the monsoon but the parent's support and dividend record lower the risk: slightly below market sensitivity (Ke 11.6%).
dcf._tgWhy: Indian crop protection and seed demand grows with farm output and prices; 5.5% nominal, below the 6% we use for faster-growing peers because ~95% of profit is paid out.
dcf._fadeGrowthWhy: Industry growth of 5-6% plus corn seed share gains.
dcf._fadeCapexWhy: Asset-light formulator and seed producer: capex (incl. leases) ~2% of sales.
